document_metadata.document_title: iSWM Criteria Manual for Site Development and Construction

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: Water Quality Protection Volume (WQv) based on 1.5 inches of rainfall (85th percentile storm), not a return-period storm. Option 2: treat WQv by reducing TSS from the development site for runoff from rainfalls up to 1.5 inches. Primary structural controls sized for WQv are expected to remove about 70–80% of annual average TSS load when designed per specifications. Methods to compute WQv referenced to Water Quality Technical Manual Section 1.2.
peak_flow_calculation_method: Streambank Protection: control 1-year, 24-hour storm (Streambank Protection Volume / SPV), including 24-hour extended detention option
Downstream assessment required for streambank protection, conveyance, and flood mitigation

evidence.excerpt: College Station — BCS Drainage Design Manual PDF 404; temporary NCTCOG iSWM / Dallas criteria
The Water Quality Protection Volume (WQv) is the runoff from the first 1.5 inches of rainfall.
Treat the Water Quality Protection Volume by reducing total suspended solids from the development site for runoff resulting from rainfall of 1.5 inches (85th percentile storm).
Modular Porous Paver Systems Infiltration rate > 0.5 inch/hr
Wet Pond Limit maximum normal pool depth to about 4 ft (dugout)

design_parameters.enrich_notes: Criteria Manual references Site Development Controls Technical Manual for detailed design criteria. WQv is first 1.5 in rainfall (85th percentile). Primary controls target 70–80% annual TSS removal. Table 3.17/3.4 list practice-specific depth-to-water-table (e.g., bioretention 2 ft, infiltration trenches 4 ft) and infiltration minimum >0.5 in/hr. Proprietary systems require manufacturer data and independent third-party verification (TARP, TAPE, or others cited in TriSWM appendix).
